page: Microsoft Azure D128ads_v7 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. The virtual machine provides 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The memory footprint stands at 512.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include instruction set support for AVX-512 (f, vnni, and bf16) as well as hardware cryptographic extensions. An integrated 7560 GB local NVMe SSD array is bundled with the instance for temporary high-speed scratch space, though it includes no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistently high throughput across dense compute, memory, and storage scenarios. In multi-core evaluation, the instance achieved a stress-ng score of 233122.22 and a PassMark CPU score of 133871.81, placing it in the top decile. Read memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks reached 389.75 GB/sec alongside 188.06 GB/sec in uncached writes. Database and caching workloads exhibit substantial execution capacity, evidenced by PassMark database operations scoring 39671.83 and Redis SET handling 177.38 million operations per second. CPU-based machine learning inference with AVX-512 VNNI reaches 68.48 tokens per second on 7B models.

The bundled 7.5 TB NVMe disk provides strong qualitative cost efficiency by avoiding external network block storage fees for intermediate data pipelines, build artifacts, or transient database indexes. However, the lack of discrete hardware acceleration limits heavy AI training, and the ephemeral nature of local NVMe disks requires reliable remote persistence layers. The configuration is suited for high-concurrency database deployments, large in-memory caching tiers, parallel data transformations, static web delivery clusters, and CI/CD compilation workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D128ads_v7 is an enterprise general-purpose instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs on 64 physical cores using AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at 4.5 GHz. It includes 512.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 4.0 GB per core balance, and packages 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The AMD architecture supports AVX-512 extensions and vector neural network instructions, driving high single-thread and parallel performance. Benchmark profiles highlight top-tier multi-threaded compute, handling 177.38 million Redis operations per second and 107.2 GB/sec static web throughput. Without dedicated GPU hardware, its processing power remains focused on large-scale scalar and vectorized CPU calculations. The bundled high-capacity NVMe array enhances efficiency for heavy scratch space and transient indexing without ancillary storage attachments. The instance fits high-concurrency relational databases, large in-memory datastores, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and demanding ETL workloads.
